item.title: Liverpool set for double injury boost ahead of Arsenal clash
item.description: Liverpool set for double injury boost ahead of Arsenal clash Liverpool vs Arsenal: Szoboszlai Injury Update Ahead of Anfield Test Liverpool do not get many easy afternoons, and Sunday will not be one of them. Arsenal head to Anfield in what looks like another serious examination for Andoni Iraola and his side, fresh from a draining Carabao Cup tie against Chelsea that went all the way to penalties. Liverpool got through it, which is what matters. The job now is recovery, selection and finding the right balance against the defending champions. Iraola rotated in midweek, handed chances to younger players and got the result. Against Arsenal, the expectation is that experience returns, if fitness allows. Szoboszlai Injury Boost for Liverpool The main talking point is Dominik Szoboszlai. The midfielder has missed Liverpool’s last three matches after being forced off against Brentford, and he has not yet returned to full team training. That is the hard fact. The more encouraging part is that he is back on the grass, which at least puts him back in the conversation. Iraola did not overplay it, and that is probably wise. “I think Szoboszlai and Munoz have a chance but we still have two days. I think they have a chance, yes.” That tells you exactly where things stand. There is hope, but no certainty. Photo: IMAGO Anfield Selection Decisions Against Arsenal Munoz is in the same bracket, available possibly, guaranteed not at all. For Liverpool, that matters because Arsenal are the sort of opponent who punish weak links, tired legs and makeshift solutions. The Chelsea game served its purpose. Liverpool progressed and protected some senior players. Now comes the bigger test. If Szoboszlai is fit enough to make the squad, even from the bench, it gives Iraola another serious option in a game where energy, ball carrying and control in midfield could decide everything. That is where Liverpool are right now, waiting on fitness checks and trying to turn a positive midweek result into something far more significant at Anfield.

item.description: Nov 10, 2024; Landover, Maryland, USA; Washington Commanders head coach Dan Quinn (L) congratulates Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels (5) after a touchdown drive against the Pittsburgh Steelers during the first half at Northwest Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Geoff Burke-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con The Philadelphia Eagles are riding a five-game losing streak entering Sunday Night Football against the Washington Commanders, a team they beat in the season opener. Can the Birds win a game for the first time since September 20? In order to preview this Week 8 NFC East battle, I reached out to our enemies over at Hogs Haven . The amicable Andrew Y kindly kindly took the time to answer my questions about this upcoming battle. Let’s take a look at the answers. 1 – In our Q&A exchange ahead of Week 1 , you said that the Commanders are “ one of the most boom-bust teams in the NFL.” There’s clearly been more bust than boom so far. What’s the biggest reason why? In short, I would say: injuries, two rookie coordinators figuring out how to call plays, and poor preparation and in-game decision making that I mostly blame on HC Dan Quinn. I should also throw in that GM Adam Peters deserves some blame for botching the Center situation in the offseason by starting week 1 with career backup IOL Nick Allegretti as our starting Center. On the plus side for Peters, he found a serviceable Center off the scrapheap in Lucas Patrick who has started at Center since week 3. In terms of injuries, the Commanders’ week 5 injury report had 23 players on it. I don’t remember seeing another injury report that long! In terms of the coordinators, we knew it was going to be risky having two coordinators who have never called plays in the NFL before and that is bearing out. On defense, DC Daronte Jones is trying to implement the complicated and almost unique Brian Flores defense from Minnesota. The defense is difficult to implement because it requires players to be very versatile, with even DTs occasionally dropping into coverage and CBs blitzing the QB. A heavily favored James Madison held a double-digit lead in the first half. The Sun Belt opponent caught up and forced overtime. The Dukes finished scoreless on their overtime possession. And the underdog drilled a walkoff field goal to complete the upset. That same script that James Madison followed in its Thursday, Oct. 22 matchup at Appalachian State was copied and pasted for its Thursday, Oct. 29 showdown against Troy. Five days after losing to winless ULM at home, Troy rebounded in magnificent fashion, stunning the reigning Sun Belt champions 24-21 on the road and snapping James Madison’s 12-game home winning streak. James Madison started the game on fire, scoring three touchdowns on its first three possessions to manufacture a 21-7 advantage. However, all of the offensive momentum halted in the second quarter. item.description: Dortmund's Polish striker Robert Lewando - AFP Relive the 2012 DFB Cup final where Borussia Dortmund dismantled Bayern Munich to secure their first-ever domestic double. It was a night defined by clinical finishing and the arrival of a new power in German football. On 12 May 2012, the Olympiastadion in Berlin became the theatre for a shift in the tectonic plates of German football. Dortmund, already crowned Bundesliga champions, arrived in the capital seeking a historic double. Bayern, bruised by their inability to stop the Westphalian surge, viewed the DFB Cup final as a necessary reclamation of their natural order. What followed was not a contest of equals, but a 5-2 clinical dismantling that remains the high-water mark of the Jurgen Klopp era. Kagawa sets the tone and the penalty exchange Dortmund's Japanese forward Shinji Kagaw Klopp’s Dortmund unleashed pure chaos right from the opening whistle, suffocating Bayern with a devastating masterclass in high-octane transition football. It took just three minutes for the pressure cooker to explode. Pouncing on a catastrophic defensive blunder from the Bavarians, Jakub Blaszczykowski picked his spot and squared across for Shinji Kagawa to slide a clinical finish past a helpless Manuel Neuer. The stadium detonated into absolute pandemonium, swept up in a deafening sea of black-and-yellow belief that had the German giants rocked to their core before they had even settled. Bayern refused to roll over, clawing their way back into the blockbuster clash when Arjen Robben held his nerve from 12 yards, dispatching a 25th-minute penalty to silence the roaring Dortmund faithful. Yet any hope of a Bavarian resurgence was short-lived, with momentum swinging violently back the other way. item.title: Chelsea manager Alonso dismisses talk of Estevao loan deal
item.description: Chelsea midfielder Estevao (Adrian Dennis) Xabi Alonso said Friday there had been no discussions about loaning out Estevao as the Brazilian teenager struggles to force his way into the Chelsea manager's first-team plans. The 19-year-old provided some rare highlights during a largely forgettable campaign for the Blues last season that saw Liam Rosenior sacked as Chelsea boss in April. But he has yet to start in the Premier League under Alonso, with Estevao having played just 172 minutes of first-team football so far this season. The rising star remained an unused substitute as Chelsea were knocked out of the League Cup by Liverpool in a penalty shoot-out on Wednesday, with his path into the starting side blocked by Alonso's favoured front three of Morgan Rogers, Cole Palmer and Joao Pedro. Nevertheless, Alonso -- speaking ahead of Chelsea's match at home to Manchester United in the Premier League on Saturday -- said of Estevao: "Sure, he will play. The season is long and there will be moments for everyone. "He will have his games, his minutes. We are still early in the season but he will be there." As for the prospects of former Palmeiras favourite Estevao leaving Stamford Bridge on loan when the transfer window re-opens in January, Alonso said: "No discussions about (a loan)." Chelsea will be eager to return to winning ways against a struggling United after defeats by Liverpool and Tottenham. jdg/dmc

item.title: Atlético reactivate Lisandro interest amid Man United contract update
item.description: MADRID, SPAIN - OCTOBER 13: Lisandro Martinez of Manchester United controls the ball during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between Atletico de Madrid and Manchester United at Estadio Metropolitano on October 13, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) | Getty Images Manchester United center-back Lisandro Martínez is poised to leave the beleaguered English giants in 2027 — and Atlético Madrid are one of the teams interested in signing him, per a new report. According to Edu Burgos in Diario AS, Lisandro’s contract at United has a mutual option that either side can trigger to extend the deal for another year. However, neither Lisandro nor his current club wants to trigger the extension clause, especially after the player tore into club management following United’s 2-0 loss at Atlético earlier this month. Lisandro Martínez no renovaría su contrato con el Manchester United. Acaba en junio de 2027 y no se ejecutaría la opción del +1. Atlético de Madrid y Barcelona entran a la carrera por su contratación. A partir de enero puede negociar con cualquier club. @diarioas … — Eduardo Burgos (@edu17burgos) October 30, 2026 It is precisely Atlético who are positioned to step up their longstanding interest in “Licha” when the 28-year-old is able to speak to other clubs in January, Burgos writes. “Given his quality and (non-existent) price, Lisandro is a real gem in such an inflated market,” Burgos said. “In fact, ‘Cuti’ Romero threw him a lifeline in an interview on the Edul brothers ‘ YouTube channel. He stated categorically: ‘Lisandro Martínez,’ when asked ‘a player I would bring to my club?’” Christian Romero asked which Argentine player he wishes Atlético Madrid would sign: "Lisandro Martínez." [ @losedul ] pic.twitter.com/2Td85bOf5f — utdreport (@utdreport) October 27, 2026 Look, Lisandro is a good defender. A technically-sound left-footed center-back with a World Cup win on his resume isn’t easy to find, and one available on a Bosman is a rarity indeed. Further, he has the same nationality as Romero, Julián Alvarez and Diego Simeone. Of course he’s going to be linked with Atleti; he’s aggressive and he’s Argentine. However, Lisandro’s inconsistency and short stature (he’s 5’9”) make me nervous, and even if he hadn’t spent part of his prime rotting at United, where would he play at Atleti? Is he going to displace Dávid Hancko? No. Hancko is just as comfortable in possession. Is he going to displace Álex Grimaldo? Also no. Is he going to play in defensive midfield? I guess he could, but that doesn’t strike me as ideal. Still, Atleti are understandably interested in what happens here. Burgos reports that Barcelona are interested in Lisandro too — and it seems to me he is more likely to end up at Camp Nou instead of the Metropolitano.

item.title: Kevin Cash reveals message to Rays after Milwaukee Brewers win World Series
item.description: The Milwaukee Brewers made quick work of the Tampa Bay Rays in five games to capture the World Series title, leaving Kevin Cash and his team just short of the championship. Despite the disappointment, the Rays manager took pride in what his players accomplished throughout the season. In his postgame interview with Ken Rosenthal, Cash revealed the message he shared with the team after their loss. A tough ending to a very impressive season. @RaysBaseball Manager Kevin Cash joins @Ken_Rosenthal after the Game 5 loss. pic.twitter.com/1FccMelSsq — FOX Sports: MLB (@MLBONFOX) October 29, 2026 “How incredibly grateful we are for what they did for the last seven months. It’s a special group. We came up short. Congrats to the Brewers and the entire organization. The guys are hurting right now, but they can see how special of a group this was and can really appreciate it in a tough moment like this,” commented the Rays manager. Kevin Cash’s Rays against the Brewers Oct 28, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Tampa Bay Rays manager Kevin Cash speaks in a press conference before game five of the 2026 World Series against the Milwaukee Brewers at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Cash’s decision to give Nick Martinez the Game 1 start instead of playoff standout Drew Rasmussen failed to pay off, as Martinez took the loss. However, the Rays’ struggles on the mound extended beyond that choice. Rasmussen and Freddy Peralta also couldn’t deliver wins in their respective outings, leaving Tampa Bay facing an insurmountable 3-0 deficit in the series. The Rays avoided a clean sweep by taking Game 4, giving their fans a consolation victory. However, Milwaukee put an end to the series in the next game, with Jacob Misiorowski delivering another impressive start to help the Brewers secure the championship. Oct 28, 2026; St. Petersburg, Florida, USA; Brewers players celebrate with the Commissioner’s Trophy after defeating the Tampa Bay Rays in game five to win the 2026 World Series at Tropicana Field. Mandatory Credit: Nathan Ray Seebeck-Imagn Images Although the World Series ended in disappointment, Kevin Cash has plenty of reasons to appreciate what his Rays accomplished. The team ended its recent postseason absence and captured the AL East crown for the first time since 2021. Still, falling short on baseball’s biggest stage for the second time leaves Cash and Tampa Bay with plenty to reassess as they prepare for another championship push. item.title: Not all signs are allowed on ESPN's College GameDay at IU. Why not?
item.description: One of the hallmarks of ESPN's College GameDay each weekend is the chippy, funny and outrageous handmade signs fans bring to the tailgate that are visible throughout the broadcast. However, not all signs are welcome on TV. This weekend, the popular pregame show is headed to Indiana University and will host its show in the heart of campus at the Showalter Fountain . On its panel are sports personalities including former Colts punter Pat McAfee, former University of Alabama football coach Nick Saban and analyst Kirk Herbstreit. Indiana basketball legend Isiah Thomas will predict college football games as the guest picker . Recently, the show's longstanding sign policies have been questioned for excluding certain messages. According to its policies, signs cannot be vulgar, religious or political. They also cannot include the URL of a website. Oversized signs and ones connected to poles are also not allowed. All fans' signs are inspected before they can enter the broadcast's taping area, and those violating the rules will be removed. To get in, fans often arrive on campus in the early morning hours and line up outside the set. ESPN staff let fans in on a first-come, first-serve basis. However, your chippy sign is not protected under the First Amendment if you're trying to be on TV. Though IU must abide by the First Amendment as a public university, ESPN's filming area is a private event, not a public forum, and the network has near-total editorial control over the space, according to a Freedom Forum analysis . The restrictions must be reasonable and viewpoint neutral, which the First Amendment education organization said ESPN's rules are. "The First Amendment is getting momentarily benched," First Amendment Specialist Alex Morey of Freedom Forum wrote. The university does need to maintain adequate space for First Amendment-protected activity elsewhere. Outside the filming area, a vulgar, religious or political sign is usually fair game and protected speech. When the GameDay broadcast visited Bloomington in the past, signs said "Nebraska's playbook is just a corn maze," "Hoosier Daddy," and "Wannabe Big (Ten) school." Some signs featured on GameDay over the years have generated controversy, including a raunchy sign at the University of Southern California, another referencing the Trail of Tears at Oklahoma State University, and one making light of former Ohio State University coach Urban Meyer’s health issues. The broadcast often attends the most anticipated games, and the network announces its next destination the Sunday prior. The team could return to Indiana next week for the top-five matchup between the University of Miami and the University of Notre Dame. The two teams have a history that could test ESPN's sign-making rules. item.title: Prince Fielder has the best perspective on the Brewers World Series win
item.description: Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images | Getty Images There is nothing like a first-time winner. Earlier this week the Milwaukee Brewers won the World Series and in the process earned the franchise’s first-ever championship. The Brewers are winners forever now and have the 2026 team to thank for that. But just because it was this year’s club that crossed that threshold hardly means that elite baseball hasn’t been played in Milwaukee before. We are talking about one of Major League Baseball’s most prolific franchises that simply did not have the thing that many people believe you have to have. Once upon a time Milwaukee boasted the thing in the big leagues at the time in Prince Fielder. Watching Brewers legends like Fielder live through this team’s experience from their perspective was interesting for baseball fans everywhere, and on Friday morning I was able to talk to him about that and a host of other things (including his once-upon-a-time commitment to play college baseball for Pat Murphy’s Arizona State Sun Devils). At both the beginning and end of our conversation I asked Prince about this year’s team and about something he specifically said about them throughout the run. Prince was on local news and was asked about his contributions to the Brewers and how he was a part of the group who helped lay the foundation for what they just became. He, respectfully, told the interviewer that he had nothing to do with this year’s team. He said he obviously played a role with the franchise, but that he had his time and this time belonged to this year’s group. It isn’t often that you see such powerful perspective like that in sports. It takes a high level of humility to be able to reach that point and I was really impressed with Prince’s thoughts for that reason. Near the end of our interview I wanted to know what he would take away from this whole run given his unique mindset and he said that he’ll recall how nice it was to be regarded by everyone as it unfolded. He said he appreciated the sentiment from Brewers fans, baseball fans at large really, and how they connected what he did during his time with the franchise to what Pat Murphy’s group just accomplished. Memories are a powerful thing in sports and Prince helped a lot of fans create some new ones on Friday as the Brewers celebrated their title. He teamed up with Budweiser to help distribute some truly one-of-one pieces of memorabilia… this stuff is unreal. item.description: Eddie Howe has been out of work since leaving Newcastle United in the summer [Getty Images] When Sir Jim Ratcliffe became a co-owner of Manchester United in 2024, much of the narrative centred on his desire to rebuild the club around a British core. Given the expense of buying homegrown players, and the difficulties Michael Carrick - the first permanent British managerial appointment of the Ineos era - has faced this season, perhaps Ratcliffe is rethinking. But if Carrick fails to stop the rot and loses his job, United are already considering the merits of appointing another British coach - albeit one who is more experienced. That Eddie Howe is a contender for a job that remains one of the most high-profile in world football isn't hard to fathom. Speak to those who have worked alongside Howe and they describe a man whose track record of improving players is a direct result of his relentless approach on the training field. They will also tell you Howe is someone who places an unwavering importance on the methodology of setting a winning culture. Howe may lack experience at one of the traditional top-six clubs, but his body of work at Bournemouth and Newcastle is impressive. Having been appointed Bournemouth boss with the club facing relegation from League Two in January 2009, Howe led them to the Premier League in 2015. He went on to establish the Cherries as a top-flight club before leaving - for a second time - in 2020. In 2021, Howe was appointed Newcastle manager. He led them from relegation trouble to qualification for the Champions League on two occasions and won the EFL Cup - the club's first trophy in 56 years - in 2025. Former United players Paul Scholes and Nicky Butt also fell short of providing their backing to Howe on their podcast, though it is worth pointing out they spoke in favour of the 48-year-old's potential appointment when Ruben Amorim was sacked in January. The Dylan Larkin saga in Detroit has reached a boiling point, with the former Red Wings captain now officially sitting out until his trade request is fulfilled. Several teams have circled the situation, but one franchise has emerged as the most aggressive suitor. The question is whether their best pitch will be enough. According to Elliotte Friedman's latest 32 Thoughts column, the Minnesota Wild's current offer for Larkin centres on prospect Danila Yurov, an additional veteran roster player, and what Friedman colourfully described as a "Costco of first-round picks." Wild general manager Bill Guerin reportedly believes this package represents the strongest bid on the table right now, even if it may not perfectly align with what Detroit is seeking. https://x.com/FriedgeHNIC/status/2116193965590360205 The disconnect between the two sides appears significant. Sources with knowledge of Minnesota's thinking told Daily Face-off that the Red Wings are being "unrealistic" in their asking price. The Wild have reportedly dangled Yurov as the centrepiece of discussions for some time, but that alone has not been enough to satisfy interim Detroit GM Shawn Horcoff. https://x.com/DailyFaceoff/status/2116168873036673066 Larkin's production this season has not helped his trade value. He managed just two goals and six points through 10 games before being suspended for sitting out until moved. Wild sources reportedly indicated there is little appetite to sweeten their offer given those underwhelming numbers. Another potential wrinkle involves the Philadelphia Flyers, who have reportedly expressed willingness to act as a third-party facilitator. The Flyers could absorb winger Yakov Trenin's $3.5 million AAV contract to help Minnesota manage the salary-cap implications of acquiring Larkin. The gap between what Minnesota is offering and what Detroit wants remains wide at this time.
